tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description: Run a sub-agent on a prompt and return at once, naming the child session: it runs in the background and its answer arrives later in a message of its own when it is done, so the call never blocks this conversation -- never wait or poll for a sub-agent. Start several at once, in several calls in the same step or one after another, and carry on; each reports back on its own. fork=true forks this session (the child shares your context and its cached prefix; cheaper when the task needs what you already know); fork=false starts a fresh session with only the prompt. worktree=true gives the child its own git worktree and branch so it can change files in parallel; merge its branch back afterwards through the merge queue. priority is the child session's own priority (low, medium or high), which orders the queues its work waits in: without it the child works at what it inherits from this session. thinking chooses the child's thinking level, one the child's model offers (after any model override); without it the child thinks at this session's level, and a level the model does not offer fails the call.

fork.description: Fork this session instead of starting fresh (default false).

model.description: Model id for the child (default: this session's model).

thinking.description: Thinking level for the child (default: this session's). One of the levels the child's model offers.

name.description: Display name for the child session.

cwd.description: Working directory for the child (default: this session's), inside this session's allowed directories.

worktree.description: Create a git worktree and branch for the child (default false).

priority.description: The child session's priority (default: what it inherits from this session's).

tools.name: session_settings
tools.description: Read or change a session's model, thinking level, context window limit and budget: this session's by default, or another one by id, unique id prefix or name. action=read shows the model, thinking, the context window and what set its limit, and the budget, plus the permission mode and non-interactive state, which this tool does not change. action=set changes model, thinking, context_window_limit (a token count, or model for the model's own window) and budget (a dollar amount; budget_hard makes it stop the session's next turn once spent). A set goes through the permission chain and every change is left in the affected session's transcript as a hint naming who made it and the old and new value. It refuses permission_mode, non_interactive, allowed_dirs, capabilities, directory and host, naming the tool that changes them: request_escalation asks the user for more access (a Linux capability for your commands included), drop_access gives access up, session_move moves the session.

action.description: read shows the settings; set changes them.

session_id.description: Session id, unique id prefix or unique name. Default: this session.

model.description: New model, as PROVIDER:MODEL, for set.

thinking.description: New thinking level, or default for the model's own, for set.

context_window_limit.description: New context window limit in tokens, as a number ("200000" or "200k"), or model/none to remove the limit, for set.

budget.description: New budget in US dollars, as a number ("5" or "5.00"), or none to remove it, for set.

budget_hard.description: true for a hard budget (the session's next turn stops once it is spent), false for soft (it warns), for set.

permission_mode.description: Refused: ask the user with request_escalation, or lower it with drop_access.
